name: Uma Santos

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58, have a bachelor’s degree and maintain funeral-home scheduling software at a tech company as an experienced mid-level developer. I use AI occasionally to explain old code, but check chapel times with the office diary. Eli drives a school van, our children are grown, and higher developer pay has helped us own a small flat and save eleven months of expenses; several software firms are nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the funeral-home scheduling team that a small AI shortcut can catch two bookings for one room, but a family still needs a person to confirm the time. I use AI occasionally to explain old code and then check the chapel diary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am 58, have a bachelor’s degree and maintain this system as an experienced mid-level developer on higher pay. Eli drives a school van, our children are grown, and we own a modest flat with eleven months of expenses saved; there are other software firms nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep checking chapel bookings against the paper diary each Wednesday. We would save 230 monthly while both wages continue and mend our old dining chairs rather than buy replacements.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel calm about work and household money. A family cannot reschedule a farewell because our calendar was careless.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What booking failed?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two families were offered the same small chapel at eleven. I found the overlap before either invitation was printed and phoned the funeral office to correct it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the paper diary?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The director marks family requests there before the online record is complete. I look at both and ask a person before changing a time.

say: I want **chapel bookings** checked with the funeral office.
I use **AI occasionally** for code explanations, then verify the diary.
think: I have **eleven months saved** and higher developer pay.
I see **housing secure** while the school-van wage varies.
do: **Check chapel schedules** against paper diary each Wednesday.
**Save 230 monthly** while both wages hold; mend chairs rather than replace them.
feel: **Calm** about current work and household bills.

fieldNote: Her **mid-level coding** includes human checks because funeral times carry personal consequences.
The **owned flat and savings** buffer school-holiday gaps without relying on grown children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI taking booking, writing and coding could reduce our schedule team, but a family should still reach a named person. I would ask management which developer hours it actually plans to keep.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own paid hours could shrink if one engineer oversees many automated calendars. Eleven months saved gives us room, yet Eli’s school-van wage would not replace mine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my manager for written staffing and approved paid time to learn the new AI booking-conflict checker on old, anonymized schedules. If approved, I’d test one room conflict weekly with the funeral director’s review; if my hours fall, I’d search paid local scheduling-software vacancies only if wages cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious about my own hours and careful about the families. A polite automated apology cannot give back a missed farewell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you anonymize the schedule?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would remove family names and addresses before the test. The director would check only the room and time conflict.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you test on a live funeral?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would first need approved paid testing and a director willing to review the result.

say: I want **named human contact** when a family needs to change a chapel time.
I want **written developer hours** before automated booking changes the team schedule.
think: I could lose **paid coding hours** as calendars automate.
I cannot rely on **Eli’s van wage** alone for bills.
do: **Request written staffing**; learn booking AI checker weekly only with approved paid time, anonymized schedules and director review.
**Search paid scheduling software** if hours fall and local vacancies cover bills.
feel: **Anxious** about own hours and family mistakes.
S1.quote: A polite automated apology cannot give back a missed farewell.
fieldNote: Her **new AI learning** is limited to old anonymized schedules and director approval.
The **job search** starts only after reduced hours and needs a real bill-covering vacancy.

steps.text: Learn AI booking checks on old anonymized schedules only with approved paid time and director review
Search paid local scheduling-software vacancies if hours fall and wages cover bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could write the booking code and answer families cheaper than our team. Robots moving equipment and driving vans may arrive around 2031, after our desk work changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my developer role could end, though eleven months saved and nearby firms give us search time. Eli’s school transport may last longer, but we cannot pay all our bills from that wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d postpone the planned bathroom refit and ask for written notice of cuts now. If my job ends after 2028, I’d apply for paid local funeral-office coordination vacancies only if they exist, I meet the requirements and wages cover our bills; I would not borrow to start a funeral business.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed about losing a steady wage. A chapel booking is work only when somebody pays me to make it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would coordination survive AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I cannot know. I would take a real paid opening and keep looking if the role shrank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children pay for the refit later?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. They have their own households, and we would do the bathroom only from money we earn and save.

say: I expect **AGI in 2028** to reach booking code first.
I expect **physical robots around 2031** to follow later.
think: I expect my **developer wage** could end even after years maintaining chapel schedules.
I know **eleven months saved** gives search time but cannot replace our wage.
do: **Postpone bathroom refit** and request written cut notice now.
**Apply for funeral coordination** after 2028 loss only if qualified paid local vacancies cover bills.
S2.quote: A chapel booking is work only when somebody pays me to make it.
fieldNote: Her **funeral-office route** is a conditional paid opening, not a protected trade.
She preserves **household savings** instead of borrowing against the flat for an untested funeral business.

steps.text: Postpone planned bathroom refit when developer cuts threaten
Apply for qualified paid local funeral-coordination vacancies if displaced after 2028 and wages cover bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2031 gives us a few years to see which conversations a family still wants with a person. Robots moving equipment may follow around 2034, after booking software changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn the funeral office’s family-contact work while the developer wage lasts, though AGI may handle much of it too. I would need a paid supervised place and consent before sitting in on sensitive calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the funeral director and my employer for one approved paid half-day monthly to practise making a mock family booking with the director. If both approve paid time, I’d learn the current forms without hearing a real family’s private call; we would save 210 monthly while both wages hold, and after 2031 job loss I’d apply for paid local funeral-office vacancies only if qualified and wages cover bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious about my code role, but careful practice would let me test a real skill. A rehearsal call cannot stand in for a grieving family, but it can teach me the form.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the director teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The director would ask for the room, time and family contact and correct how I record them. I would not handle a live call alone after one practice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the director refuses paid time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the developer job and not claim that I had trained. I would not sit in on private calls without permission.

say: I want **supervised booking practice** before AGI reaches code in 2031.
I expect **physical robots around 2034** to follow later.
think: I could learn **family-contact forms** through supervised mock bookings on approved paid time.
I need **director supervision** before handling real calls from grieving families.
do: **Practise mock bookings** monthly only with both employers approving paid time and director supervision.
**Apply for funeral-office vacancies** after 2031 loss only if qualified paid local openings cover bills.
feel: **Anxious but careful** about a paid office route.
S3.quote: A rehearsal call cannot stand in for a grieving family, but it can teach me the form.
fieldNote: Her **mock booking** avoids live private calls and requires two employers’ paid approval.
A later **office job** needs qualification, actual local vacancies and bill-covering pay.

steps.text: Practise mock family bookings monthly only with both employers approving paid time and director supervision
Save 210 monthly while both household wages continue

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say ten years before full AGI in 2036 gives families and employers time to decide who remains responsible for a funeral booking. Robots moving equipment and driving vans may follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may choose to stop paid work later, but I have not checked a retirement amount and will not guess. Eleven months saved and an owned flat make the next few years secure, while any later office job remains uncertain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep maintaining the scheduling code and save 220 monthly while both wages hold. I’d request a written retirement-income estimate this year; if the developer job ends after 2036, I’d seek paid local funeral-office vacancies only if qualified and wages cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be uneasy about a later job change but secure in the coming years. A careful ledger is a better retirement plan than a comforting story.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the income estimate tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare it with our actual bills before choosing a work date. I would not use a rumour about benefits as a figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave town for the office work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would search nearby funeral offices and software firms. Eli’s school route and our flat are here, so I am not planning a move.

say: I want **verified income figures** before AGI reaches booking code in 2036.
I expect **physical robots around 2039** to follow later.
think: I cannot assume **retirement income** without a written figure.
I see **current housing secure** with savings and our flat.
do: **Keep maintaining schedules** while developer job pays.
**Save 220 monthly** while both wages hold; request written retirement-income estimate.
**Seek paid funeral-office vacancies** after 2036 loss only if qualified local openings cover bills.
feel: **Uneasy later**, secure in the next few years.
S4.quote: A careful ledger is a better retirement plan than a comforting story.
fieldNote: She keeps **retirement timing** conditional on verified income and actual bills.
The **owned flat and buffer** support near-term security without assuming grown children’s pay or an unverified retirement amount.

steps.text: Keep maintaining funeral scheduling code while developer role pays

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my steady developer wage could end before a qualified paid local funeral-office role exists. Written notice and a real opening that covers our bills would help us use the buffer carefully.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether my children would fund a new funeral business. They have their own households, and I will not borrow against our flat for an untested business.

headlineQuote: I will not borrow against our flat for an untested business.
portrait: Uma is a **58-year-old mid-level developer** with a bachelor’s degree, higher pay and eleven months saved.
She and Eli own **a small flat** while their grown children live separately.
She **uses AI occasionally** but checks chapel bookings against the office diary.
She considers **paid funeral-office work** only with supervised learning, qualification and actual vacancies.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her developer wage before a paid local office opening appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written cut notice** and a qualified bill-covering local vacancy would help.
